title: The Second Letter of John
lead: The shortest book of the Bible by number of verses (13): a letter from "the Elder" to "the chosen lady and her children," a church or a Christian household. It urges them to keep the old command to love each other and warns them not to take into the house teachers who do not confess "Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh" (2 John 1:7, 10). Its authorship, its addressee and how far its rule against welcoming false teachers reaches have been debated since the early church.

sections.b: Greeting from the Elder to the chosen lady and her children, "whom I love in truth" (1:1-3); joy at children walking in truth and the command to love each other, had "from the beginning" (1:4-6); deceivers who do not confess Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh, and the rule not to take such a teacher into the house or say "Greetings!" to him (1:7-11); a visit hoped for, and greetings from "the children of your chosen sister" (1:12-13).

The lady is a church pictured as a woman, a Christian woman and her family, or a woman named Kyria or Electa; the book page and the notes give each view. The letter shares its wording with 1 John (love, truth, the antichrist, "coming in the flesh") and its opening and ending with 3 John. Eusebius counted 2 and 3 John among the disputed books, and some in Jerome's day gave them to "John the presbyter" rather than the apostle. Tradition places the Elder at Ephesus.
